fullPassage:
Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing, which has been a culturally significant practice of the Maori for thousands of years. It is not only decorative but also symbolic of an individual’s journey from their past to their present. Each curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a person’s whakapapa (genealogy), social positions, and personal accomplishments. This explains why no two tā moko designs look the same. Traditionally, the Maori have considered the head to be the most sacred part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their faces. Men typically wear tā moko over their entire faces, while women have it on their lips and chins. The Maori start getting these designs in their teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines and shapes are added to their tattoos to reflect their life experiences. Tattooing traditionally held great importance as a rite of passage throughout their lives. Although tā moko is less common these days, it is still practiced today by Maori people, who hope to preserve their traditions and heritage for the next generation.

The phone rang, and it was my dad calling from my hometown, Waituhi. “Can you take a week off?” he asked. “Your Nani Tama wants you here.” “But Dad!” I answered. “My boss won’t let me take any more time off.” The phone went silent, and then I heard my grandfather say faintly, “I need your help, Grandson. I must go to Murupara to finish the whakapapa. Drive me there. Hurry, I may not have much time.” I just knew I had no choice. “All right, Nani,” I replied with a sigh. “I’ll come.”

For some time, my grandfather had been busy writing down the village genealogy, known as the whakapapa. The whakapapa had been in his old house. But then came the night of the fire, which ran through the house and destroyed our past. In only one night, everything we knew was gone. Nani Tama, in despair, went to stay with his daughter, my Auntie Hiraina.

Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past, Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his shaky hands. He chanted the names of the ancestors, joining the past to the present once more. The village went quiet and listened to his chanting. His voice traveled along the lines of our genealogy, searching back across the centuries. Sometimes, there were lines that were difficult to remember. Then his voice suddenly stopped in the middle of the chant. The village waited in worried silence until the next name burst out of his mouth. It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather most of the whakapapa, but there were still missing names he needed to fill in.

When I arrived at Auntie’s place, I was shocked to see how thin Nani Tama was. “Look, Nani,” I said. “I’m not taking you anywhere. You could die on me!” Nani looked at me in anger. “You want me to die here in this room? Looking at these four walls? When the whakapapa is not yet finished?” The old man held on tightly to the side of the bed and cried out as he stood up. Every slow, painful step hurt him, but he tried to walk. I could not help but carry him to the car, and we set off with Auntie.

We traveled all night, mostly in silence, listening to Nani chanting in the darkness. It was strange but wonderful to hear him. Sometimes, he burst into a song that he had taught Auntie. They sang together, lifting up their voices to send the song flying like a bird through the sky.

Now that day seems like a dream to me. I remember the two old men sitting at the table and the soft sounds of the Maori words as they talked. All through the quiet afternoon and into the evening, they recalled missing names. I had a strange feeling that there were other people in the room. I felt as if people from the past were looking over the shoulders of the two old men to see if the work was correct.

It was early morning and still dark when we returned to Auntie’s place. All the lights were on, and the village people were waiting for us. Smiling, Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and offered it to the village. Our hearts were full because our grandfather had saved our past for us.

questions.passage: The whakapapa had been in his old house. But then came the night of the fire, __________ ran through the house and destroyed our past. In only one night, everything we knew was gone.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 선행사 the fire(사물)를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사 which가 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② which: 사물 선행사(the fire) + 주격 관계대명사
❌ ① what: 선행사 포함 → 앞에 선행사(the fire)가 있으므로 불가
❌ ③ who: 사람 선행사용
❌ ④ where: 관계부사 → 뒤에 완전한 절이 와야 함
det.tip: 선행사(사물) + which + 동사: 사물을 수식하는 주격 관계대명사

questions.passage: Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past, Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his shaky hands. He chanted the names of the ancestors, __________ the past to the present once more.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 주절(chanted)과 동시에 일어나는 부대상황 → 분사구문 joining이 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ joining: 동시동작 분사구문(현재분사)
❌ ① joined: 과거형 → 접속사 없이 두 절 연결 불가
❌ ② to join: to부정사 → 동시동작에 부적절
❌ ④ having joined: 완료 분사구문 → 동시동작이 아님
det.tip: 분사구문 (동시동작): 주절, ~ing ... → 동시에 일어나는 동작

questions.passage: When I arrived at Auntie’s place, I was shocked to see __________ thin Nani Tama was.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: "see + how + 형용사 + 주어 + 동사" 구조에서 정도/상태를 나타내는 how가 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① how: see how + 형용사(thin) + S + V → "얼마나 야위었는지"
❌ ② what: what + 명사 구조 → thin은 형용사
❌ ③ that: 접속사 → 형용사 thin과 직접 연결 불가
❌ ④ so: 부사 → see so thin은 비문
det.tip: see/know + how + 형용사 + S + V: 얼마나 ~한지 보다/알다

questions.passage: Every slow, painful step hurt him, but he tried to walk. I could not help but __________ him to the car, and we set off with Auntie.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: "could not help but + 동사원형" = ~할 수밖에 없다. carry가 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② carry: could not help but + 동사원형 → "모시고 갈 수밖에 없었다"
❌ ① carrying: cannot help + ~ing는 가능하나, but이 있으면 원형
❌ ③ to carry: 문법적 불가
❌ ④ carried: 과거형 → 원형이 필요
❌ ⑤ having carried: 완료형 → 원형이 필요
det.tip: cannot help but + 동사원형 = cannot help + ~ing = ~하지 않을 수 없다

questions.passage: We traveled all night, mostly in silence, ①<u>listening</u> to Nani chanting in the darkness. It was strange but wonderful to ②<u>hear</u> him. Sometimes, he burst into a song that he had ③<u>teaching</u> Auntie.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~③ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ teaching → taught: 과거완료(had) 뒤에는 과거분사(taught)가 와야 한다. "그가 고모에게 가르쳐 주었던 노래"
det.analysis:
❌ ③ teaching → taught: had + p.p.(과거완료) 구조
✅ ① listening: 분사구문 (동시동작) → 올바름
✅ ② hear: to부정사의 동사원형 → 올바름
det.tip: had + p.p.(과거분사): 과거완료 시제. teach → taught(과거분사)

questions.passage: For some time, my grandfather had been busy writing down the village genealogy, known as the whakapapa. The whakapapa had been in his old house. questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: "the night of the fire, which ran through the house and destroyed our past" → 화재로 과거(와카파파)가 파괴되었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 화재로 와카파파 소실: "the fire destroyed our past" 일치
❌ ① 무루파라의 노인과 함께 완성함
❌ ② "My boss won’t let me" → 기꺼이가 아님
❌ ④ "shocked to see how thin" → 건강하지 않았음
det.tip: 내용 일치: 핵심 사건(화재 → 와카파파 파괴)을 정확히 대조

ch: 손주는 기꺼이 휴가를 내고 고향에 갔다.

questions.passage: Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past, Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his shaky hands. questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: "The village went quiet and listened to his chanting" → 마을은 조용히 하고 낭송을 들었다. "무관심했다"는 반대.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ 무관심했다: 원문 "went quiet and listened" → 주의 깊게 들음
✅ ① "shaky hands" → 일치
✅ ② "lines that were difficult to remember" → 일치
✅ ③ "almost two years" → 일치
det.tip: 불일치: "listened"(경청했다) ≠ "무관심했다"

ch: 할아버지는 떨리는 손으로 와카파파를 다시 썼다.
할아버지의 낭송 중 기억나지 않는 이름이 있었다.

questions.passage: When I arrived at Auntie’s place, I was shocked to see how thin Nani Tama was. “Look, Nani,” I said. “I’m not taking you anywhere. You could die on me!” Nani looked at me in anger. “You want me to die here in this room? Looking at these four walls? When the whakapapa is not yet finished?” The old man held on tightly to the side of the bed and cried out as he stood up. Every slow, painful step hurt him, but he tried to walk. I could not help but carry him to the car, and we set off with Auntie.
questions.stem: 화자(손주)의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 처음에는 할아버지의 건강이 걱정되어 "I’m not taking you anywhere"라고 하지만, 할아버지의 강한 의지를 보고 감동받아 결국 모시고 간다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 걱정 → 감동: "You could die on me!"(걱정) → "I could not help but carry him"(감동·결심)
❌ ① 기쁨: 처음 심경이 기쁨이 아님
❌ ③ 지루함: 문맥과 무관
❌ ④ 두려움→후회: 후회 없음
❌ ⑤ 무관심: 문맥과 무관
det.tip: 심경 변화: 초반 반응(걱정/거부) → 후반 행동(감동/수용)으로 파악

questions.passage: The whakapapa had been in his old house. But then came the night of the fire, which ran through the house and destroyed our past. In only one night, everything we knew was gone. Nani Tama, in __________, went to stay with his daughter, my Auntie Hiraina.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 모든 것이 하룻밤에 사라진 후 할아버지의 감정은 절망(despair)이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ despair(절망): "everything we knew was gone" → 절망적 상황
❌ ① relief(안도): 상황과 반대
❌ ② excitement(흥분): 부정적 상황에 부적절
❌ ③ curiosity(호기심): 문맥과 무관
det.tip: in despair = 절망에 빠져 — 모든 것을 잃은 상황의 감정

questions.passage: For some time, my grandfather had been busy writing down the village __________, known as the whakapapa.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 와카파파(whakapapa)는 마을의 계보(genealogy)이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② genealogy(계보): whakapapa = 가문의 혈통/계보
❌ ① mythology(신화): 계보가 아님
❌ ③ geography(지리): 무관
❌ ④ archaeology(고고학): 무관
det.tip: genealogy = family tree = 계보, 가계도 — whakapapa의 영어 대응어

questions.passage: Traditionally, the Maori have considered the head to be the most __________ part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their faces.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 마오리족은 머리를 신체 중 가장 신성한(sacred) 부분으로 여긴다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ sacred(신성한): 얼굴에 문신하는 이유 = 머리가 가장 신성하기 때문
❌ ① ordinary(평범한): 특별한 이유가 필요
❌ ② decorative(장식적인): 이유로 부족
❌ ④ dangerous(위험한): 문맥과 무관
det.tip: sacred = 신성한, 거룩한 — "so they mainly tattoo their faces"가 결과 단서

questions.passage: The phone went silent, and then I heard my grandfather say __________ (faint), “I need your help, Grandson.”
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: faint(형용사) → faintly(부사): 동사 say를 수식하는 부사 필요. "희미하게 말하다"
det.analysis:
faint(형용사) → faintly(부사)
동사 say를 수식 → 부사 필요
faintly = 희미하게, 가냘프게
det.tip: faint → faintly / quiet → quietly / sudden → suddenly — 형용사 → -ly 부사화

questions.passage: Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing, which has been a __________ (culture) significant practice of the Maori for thousands of years.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: culture(명사) → culturally(부사): 형용사 significant를 수식하는 부사 필요. "문화적으로 중요한"
det.analysis:
culture(명사) → cultural(형용사) → culturally(부사)
형용사 significant를 수식 → 부사 필요
culturally significant = 문화적으로 중요한
det.tip: culture → cultural → culturally — 명사 → 형용사 → 부사 변환

questions.passage: For some time, my grandfather had been busy writing down the village genealogy, known as the whakapapa. The whakapapa had been in his old house. But then came the night of the fire, which ran through the house and destroyed our past.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 화재로 소실된 마을의 계보를 가리키는 마오리어 명칭을 본문에서 1단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "the village genealogy, known as the whakapapa" → 와카파파
det.analysis:
마을 계보의 마오리어 명칭 = whakapapa
"known as the whakapapa" = 와카파파라고 알려진
det.tip: "known as" = ~로 알려진 → 고유 명칭을 찾는 단서

questions.passage: Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past, Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his shaky hands. He chanted the names of the ancestors, joining the past to the present once more.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 할아버지가 낭송한 이름이 누구의 이름인지를 본문에서 1단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "He chanted the names of the ancestors" → 조상들의 이름
det.analysis:
할아버지가 낭송한 것 = the names of the ancestors
1단어 답 = ancestors
det.tip: "the names of the ancestors" = 조상들의 이름

questions.passage: Now that day seems like a dream to me. I remember the two old men sitting at the table and the soft sounds of the Maori words as they talked. All through the quiet afternoon and into the evening, they recalled missing names. I had a strange feeling that there were other people in the room. I felt as if people from the past were looking over the shoulders of the two old men to see if the work was correct.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"The narrator actually saw people from the past in the room."

det.korean: 본문: "I felt as if people from the past were looking over..." → 실제로 본 것이 아니라 마치 ~인 것처럼 느꼈다. → False
det.analysis:
❌ False: "felt as if" = 가정법 → 실제가 아닌 느낌/상상
"actually saw"(실제로 보았다)와 다름
det.tip: as if + 가정법: 실제가 아닌 상상/느낌을 표현 → "actually"와 구분
